findings.title: Node cap undercounts common Mermaid syntax, so oversized diagrams pass
quotes: An ID is a token `[A-Za-z_][\w]*` that is an endpoint of an arrow
findings.fix: parse the endpoints more strictly. Strip edge text and trailing `: ...`, split on `&` and `;`, and keep `DROP` within one line. Add tests for sequence, state, `&` and labelled-edge forms.

sources.situation: `nodes` splits each line on ARROW and keeps only parts that are a bare ID. Mermaid has several common forms whose parts are not bare IDs, so those nodes are never counted.

`Alice->>John: Hello` leaves `John: Hello` after the split, which is not an ID, so John is not counted. `A --> B & C` and `A -- text --> B` are also missed. A sequence or state diagram with more than 20 participants can pass the cap. The test covers only flowchart chains.

a sequence diagram of 25 lines `Client->>Svc1: call` through `Client->>Svc25: call`. ARROW.split gives `Client` and `Svc1: call`; `Svc1: call` fails ID.fullmatch, so nodes() returns {Client}, one node, and the 20-node check passes a 26-node diagram. The same happens to `B` in `A -- retry --> B`, because `A -- retry` is not an ID.

findings.reason: implementation-E-1-adversary: the parsing of edge text, `&`, `;` and `: ...` is now right, and the sequence, state, `&` and labelled-edge tests were added. But `DROP` still runs over the whole block, so one unbalanced `"`, `(`, `[` or `{` in a line swallows every line up to the next closer. A valid sequence message such as `Client->>Svc3: retry (see note` followed by `Client->>Svc4: ok)` loses both lines before the `:` split ever runs. Those nodes are not counted, so an oversized diagram passes the AC-5 cap, which is the original symptom. No test covers it. Fix: apply `DROP` per line, `DROP.sub("", line)` inside the loop.; implementation-E-1-consistency: the listed steps (strip `: ...`, split `&` and `;`, DROP first) and their tests are in, but `A <--> B` still drops `A` and `A --o B` drops both endpoints, so the node cap still undercounts common flowchart syntax.; implementation-E-1-correctness: the parsing is stricter and the new forms are tested, but `DROP` is still applied to the whole block and can span lines, so one unbalanced quote or bracket still hides later nodes from the cap.

findings.title: Any non-parse render failure becomes "unreachable", which skips the check and hides every later block
quotes: after which no further block is rendered
findings.fix: separate "could not run" (npx missing, fetch failure, timeout, spawn error) from "ran and rejected the diagram". Treat the second as `broken` with the first error line. Keep skipping for the first only.

sources.situation: `render` returns "broken" only when the output contains the text `Parse error`. Other genuine diagram failures fall to "unreachable", for example an unknown diagram type from a typo like `flowchar TD`, a text-only block, or a mermaid runtime error. CT-4 turns "unreachable" into the note `render skipped: the renderer could not be fetched`, exit 0, and stops rendering every later block. One bad block early in the file therefore hides all later broken diagrams, with a misleading reason. Failures to start Chromium or to download it within the 120 s timeout take the same path. AC-9 ("fails naming that block as a broken diagram") is met only for parse errors.

findings.reason: render() returns "unreachable" for any non-zero exit without "Parse error", as CT-3 says ("any other failure"). A typo such as `flowchar TD` fails with an error other than Parse error. CT-4 then turns that into the "could not be fetched" note and stops rendering later blocks, so FR-11 and AC-9 are not met for it.

findings.title: `check explainer` passes any existing file
quotes: then it fails naming that block as a broken diagram
findings.fix: make the partial state loud (a note such as `checks not built yet`), or keep `explainer` out of the CLI choices until T-3 lands.

sources.situation: `check` returns `[], []` for any `.md` file or slug that exists, including an empty file, a 21-node diagram or a broken diagram. `nio check explainer <slug>` exits 0 and prints no notes, so this is a silent pass. It is only safe if T-3 to T-5 land before anything relies on the command. The `explain.format` handling and the topic-mode distinction in CT-4 are also absent. Nothing marks the check as a stub. Unlike `explain finish`, it does not say "not built yet".

findings.title: `sections` drops `> ` lines from the walk-through and handles fences loosely
quotes: lines starting `> ` and the record lines of the Data model
findings.fix: match the closing fence to the opener, and drop `> ` only when it is the tool's own note. Implement or remove the Data model rule.

sources.situation: any prose line starting `> ` is excluded from `walk`, not only the tool's own `> Broken diagram:` notes. A long walk-through written as a block quote passes the 120-word limit, and so does an empty one (which skips the "walk-through missing" rule). The Data model record-line exclusion is not implemented. Fences:

findings.title: `render` runs `npx` from the caller's working directory
findings.fix: run with `cwd` set to the temp directory. Give the timeout case its own note.

sources.situation: `subprocess.run` has no `cwd`. `npx` prefers a matching package in the cwd's `node_modules/.bin`, so the target project's own copy of mermaid-cli would run instead of the pinned 11.4.2. If it is not pinned, the first run downloads and executes a package in a repo the tool does not control. A cold fetch of Chromium may exceed 120 s. The timeout then reports "unreachable" (see F2), and the `npx` child may leave Chromium running.

findings.title: AC-9 has no test and no check behind it
quotes: it fails naming that block as a broken diagram
findings.fix: add the `broken diagram: <title>` error to `explain.check` and the test that asserts exit 1 and the block's title. If that is planned for a later epic, drop AC-9 from this epic's coverage.

sources.situation: a diagram block with a syntax error goes through `nio check explainer`. `check` returns `[], []`, so it exits 0 and names no broken block. test_ac9_broken_block is listed at line 0 and is not in tests/test_explain.py.

findings.reason: tasks.md E-1 gives T-1 only TC-5's `nodes` assertion, and the broken-diagram check belongs to T-4 in E-2 (Serves AC-9, Test TC-14, TC-15). check() is stated as "Only the missing-file error so far". That the error and test are absent is by plan, not a defect in E-1.

findings.title: AC-5 is proven only for the node count, not for the failing check
findings.fix: add `too many nodes: <title> (<n> > 20)` to `check` and extend the test to run `nio check explainer` on a 21-node fixture, expecting exit 1 and the title. If the check part belongs to a later epic, say so in the epic's coverage.

sources.situation: a fixture explainer with a 21-node diagram is checked. `explain.check` has no `too many nodes` error, so the CLI exits 0. test_ac5_node_cap only asserts `nodes()` on strings, and its own comment says "the check part lands with T-3".

findings.reason: tasks.md T-1 says "TC-5 (its `explain.nodes` assertion only; the check part is T-3's)". The `too many nodes` error and its CLI test belong to T-3 in E-2, so E-1 does not need them.

quotes: that is an endpoint of an arrow
found.update(p.strip() for p in parts if ID.fullmatch(p.strip()))
findings.fix: take the leading ID of each arrow side (for example, match `^\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)` on each part) and add a sequence-diagram case to tests/test_explain.py.

findings.title: A node whose ID starts with `end` is skipped
findings.fix: match the keyword `end` only as the whole word (the line equal to `end`, or `end` followed by a space), say so in CT-2, and add `endpoint --> api` to the self-check.

sources.situation: the flowchart line `endpoint --> api` starts with `end`, so `line.startswith(SKIP)` is true and both `endpoint` and `api` are dropped. A 25-node flowchart whose nodes are named `endpoint1 --> endpoint2` and so on counts zero nodes and passes the cap.

findings.reason: implementation-E-1-consistency: the code now matches the whole word `end` and the self-check line is added, but CT-2 in `contracts.md` line 24 still lists `end` as a skipped line prefix and does not state the whole-word rule the fix asked for.

findings.title: Broken-diagram reason is read from both streams, not stderr
quotes: first stderr line holding Parse error
findings.fix: take the line from `r.stderr` only, as CT-3 says, or change CT-3 to say stdout or stderr and make the code and spec match.

sources.situation: when mermaid-cli writes its `Parse error` line to stdout, `render` returns that line as the reason, but CT-3 says the reason is the first stderr line. The same failing run gets a different reason from the one the spec names.

findings.title: `sections()` returns a `diagram` key that CT-1 does not list
quotes: {"title": str, "fence": str | None, "block": str | None, "walk": str, "drill": bool}
s["diagram"] = s.pop("img") or s["block"] is not None
findings.fix: add `"diagram": bool` to CT-1's Shape, or drop the key and let callers test `block` and `img` through the spec's rule.

sources.situation: a consumer written from CT-1's Shape never learns that `diagram` exists, so the CT-4 "diagram section" check would recompute it from `fence` and `block` and could disagree with `sections()` on a section that has only a `![` line.

findings.title: SKIP prefix "end" drops any line starting with an ID like endpoint
findings.fix: match `end` only as the whole line, and `subgraph` only when followed by whitespace

sources.situation: `endpoint --> db` starts with "end" and is skipped entirely, so both IDs go uncounted. The same holds for `ending`, `endUser` and similar names.

findings.title: sections leaves the Data model record lines in walk
quotes: the record lines of the Data model
findings.fix: exclude the record lines in `sections`, or state in the contract that the Data model is exempt from the walk check

sources.situation: the contract says `walk` excludes the Data model's record lines. The code strips only fenced blocks, `![` lines and `> ` lines. A long Data model section would count its records toward the 120-word walk limit that T-3 enforces, and could fail a good explainer.
